title: Claim
description:
The C3 seam contract: one claim row as emitted by the Python parse service across the JSON boundary to the backend. The consuming side validates against this SAME file. A change here must be made on both sides together, or the contract job fails.

A claim is an assertion pending verification, not a verified truth (hence claims, not facts). Nothing is emitted without a citation attached at write time, and provenance is all-or-nothing: a claim resolves to an exact span, or it is emitted with status=missing. A partial or approximate citation is never written.

canonicalAttribute.description: SIM-344: the closed canonical attribute vocabulary -- the parser's CoreAttribute enum plus two catch-alls: `operating_metric` (a real sector metric outside the core financial vocabulary) and `core_unmapped` (SIM-384; financial but unplaceable -- distinct from operating_metric so the two don't collapse into one ungroupable bucket). E2 maps a document's raw label onto one of these and stores the result in `attribute` (the raw label is kept in `attribute_raw`). Published here so both repos and every cross-claim consumer -- 3b consistency rules, scoring, cross-source matching -- key on the SAME names; a contract test keeps this enum identical to the parser's CoreAttribute so the two cannot drift.

edge.title: Edge
edge.description:
SIM-341: a within-page relationship between two claims a per-page reducer found at the extraction fan-in, sitting beside `claims` in the emitted payload (not a property of a single claim row, so it is not referenced from the Claim schema above). `from`/`to` name claims by their `claim_ref` (SIM-365) -- the stable, positional, attribute-independent id every claim carries -- not the backend's `id`, which does not exist yet at parse time. The parser only emits the edge; it never merges or drops a claim because of one -- store persistence and cross-document edges are the backend's job at ingest.

same_fact: `to` is the higher-precision source (table wins on a number); `from` is corroboration of the same real-world fact, not a duplicate to discard. contradicts: `from`/`to` disagree on value for what looks like the same fact -- neither is preferred, and the disagreement itself is what a consumer needs to see.

basis.description: Human-readable reason the reducer linked these two claims, e.g. which tiers agreed or disagreed and on what.

data_source_id.description: FK to data_sources (document identity + versioning). Assigned by the ingesting backend; the parse service cites the file by name in location.file.

claim_ref.description: SIM-365: a stable, positional, attribute-independent id the parser assigns to every claim -- {page}:{char_start}-{char_end}[#n] for a PDF span, {sheet}!{cell_ref}[#n] for XLSX, or {page}:none[#n] for a spanless claim; [#n] disambiguates claims sharing one span. Deterministic across runs and unaffected by attribute canonicalization. `edges` name their endpoints by it, and the backend keys idempotent re-ingest on it (unique per org + data_source). Distinct from the backend-assigned surrogate `id`, which does not exist at parse time.

claim_type.description: SIM-364 / FinGround (arXiv:2604.23588): the TYPE of assertion, assigned at extraction, orthogonal to the binding-audit verdicts. Verification routes on it: computational -> formula reconstruction, numerical -> exact-span, comparative/regulatory -> their own checks. Non-null with `unknown` as the explicit fallback for an un-typeable claim -- an untyped claim is skipped by type-routing, never defaulted to a wrong type. The table/XLSX tiers set it in code (numerical, or computational for a formula cell); the prose/qualitative tiers set it from the model.

entity.description: What the claim is about (company, segment, etc.).

attribute.description: The claim's field. When E2 canonicalization has run (SIM-344; `attribute_raw` is then non-null) this is a canonical value from `$defs/canonicalAttribute` (e.g. `revenue`, `gross_profit`, `ebitda`) -- NOT a camelCase/unit-suffixed label; otherwise it is the document's own label (a pre-canonicalization or qualitative claim). Cross-claim matching (3b consistency, scoring) keys on the canonical value.

attribute_raw.description: SIM-344: the document's own label for this attribute, before canonical mapping (e.g. "Revenue | 2019F"), retained alongside the canonical `attribute`. Null for a claim the canonicalization pass never reached -- e.g. a qualitative assertion, which is categorized by assertion_class instead and keeps its own attribute vocabulary.

period_year.description: Fiscal year the claim applies to, when the source states one.

period_kind.description: A=Actual, E=Estimate, P=Projected. Null when the source does not qualify the period.

value.description: Unit-normalized at write time; raw is never overwritten. The canonical number everything compares against is `normalized`.

normalized.description: After scale + unit applied, e.g. 15295000. null only when value_type is text.

scale_multiplier.description: What took raw -> normalized, e.g. 1000. Required alongside scale_source for every value_type that has a magnitude -- see the scale allOf block. NOTE: JSON Schema cannot express arithmetic across fields, so it cannot check that normalized == parse(raw) * scale_multiplier. That invariant is enforced by scale.scale_invariant_holds, asserted in the contract test and on the emit path. Validating this document against the schema alone does NOT establish that the magnitude is right.

scale_source.description: HOW scale was determined. explicit_in_value: the token stated its own multiplier ("$4.8M", "27.3%"). column_header / page_header: read from a scale phrase, which is recorded with it. assumed_1x: nothing was found and the magnitude is UNKNOWN -- it must stay distinguishable from a known 1x, and raises the scale_assumed flag. not_applicable: a multiplier is meaningless for this value_type (a headcount, a date), which is a KNOWN 1x and raises nothing. Conflating the last two destroys the distinction this field exists to preserve: a count that borrowed explicit_in_value was claiming its own text stated a scale it never stated.

value_type.description: Drives tolerance selection at comparison time (Verify / golden-set diff). Only currency is scaled by a column/page header.

location.description:
Typed union by kind. PDF => page/char span; XLSX => sheet/cell_ref; DOCX => paragraph/char span. One claims spine stores all three: the format-specific columns are null per row.

The location says WHERE WE LOOKED; the char span says WHERE IT IS. The locator (page / sheet+cell_ref / paragraph) is always required, because a claim always knows where it was searched for. The span is required the moment the claim asserts it found something -- see the all-or-nothing rule in allOf. Where a span exists it is exact, zero tolerance.

file.description: Source filename — debug/human-readable only. The canonical document identity is the top-level data_source_id; the claims table has no file column.

page.description: PDF page index, not printed footer.

bbox.description: Docling's native coordinate system, coord_origin preserved verbatim — no highlight-UI decision is smuggled in here.

file.description: Source filename — debug only; canonical identity is data_source_id.

cell_ref.description: e.g. B14. A merged cell cites its anchor (top-left) cell; no merge range is persisted.

file.description: Source filename — debug only; canonical identity is data_source_id.

paragraph.description: Paragraph index; maps to the claims table's DOCX-only `paragraph` column.

char_start.description: DOCX is a linear text stream, so a claim cites an exact span exactly like PDF — a paragraph index alone is not a citation. Required, per all-or-nothing provenance.

status.description:
How much trust the claim has earned. The parse service emits only the reachable subset:
- `proposed` — citation attached, not yet checked. Covers PDF/DOCX prose and tables, AND an XLSX formula cell: the cell reference is byte-exact, but the value is pending, because this service never executes formulas (re-execution happens outside it) and the file's own cached result is never trusted as a substitute.
- `cited` — nothing left to check. At parse time this is reachable only for a literal XLSX cell (`direct_read`): reading the bytes IS the verification. A formula reaches `cited` later, once re-executed (`formula_reexecution`).
- `missing` — no citation exists in the source.
Verify moves proposed -> cited|rejected; the corroboration pass moves cited -> conflicted|inconclusive|partially_verified|verified. An extractor must never assert cited for a value it has not had checked — which is why an unexecuted formula is `proposed`, not `cited`.

verification_method.description: HOW the claim earned citation-level trust. Null before anything has been checked (status=proposed|rejected|missing); required once status is cited or later. direct_read = a literal XLSX cell; formula_reexecution = a workbook formula independently recomputed.

chunk_id.description: The chunk the quote was read from. Agent-self-reported and validated by substring match within that chunk only. Set together with char_start/char_end, or not at all.

table_group_id.description: Groups fragments of one logical table split across pages.

fragment_order.description: Order of this fragment within table_group_id.

claim_kind.description: Which extraction contract produced this claim. Absent or 'quantitative': the value carries a magnitude, or carries none because the magnitude guard could not read one (see the magnitude_unparseable flag). 'qualitative': the claim IS a text assertion by design -- value.normalized is null on purpose, not by failure. Optional and absent-means-quantitative, so every row written before this field existed stays valid.

assertion_class.description: For a qualitative claim, which kind of assertion it is. Null otherwise.

allOf.$comment: All-or-nothing provenance, enforced. A claim that is not `missing` asserts it FOUND something, so it must carry the exact span proving where. Only `missing` -- which asserts the opposite -- may omit it. Previously the span was unconditionally required, which forced a missing claim to fabricate char_start=0/char_end=0: a zero span reads as a citation to the top of the page, so the schema was mandating exactly the approximate citation this rule exists to forbid. XLSX is exempt because a cell reference IS the whole citation; there is no sub-cell span to give.

The other half of all-or-nothing: a `missing` claim asserts that nothing was found, so it must not carry a span AT ALL -- not even char_start=0/char_end=0. A zero span is not an absence, it is a citation to the first character of the page, and a consumer highlighting it would point the user at unrelated text while the claim says nothing was found. Requiring the span unconditionally is what produced that fabrication in the first place, so both halves are enforced here: found => span, missing => no span.
Mirrors the claims-table CHECK: verification_method records how trust was earned, so it must be present once a claim has actually been checked.

A value with a magnitude must say what took raw to normalized, and how that was determined. Both, or the pair proves nothing: a claim carrying scale_source=page_header with no multiplier asserts a header was read while withholding what it said, and a multiplier with no source is a bare number nobody can audit. This was NOT enforced, and the gap was not theoretical -- a claim reading raw="$15,295", normalized=999, scale_source="page_header" and no multiplier validated clean, a 15,000x error the contract had no opinion about. Every defect found in the July 2026 parser audit was a scale error of exactly this shape.

Exempt when there is no magnitude to describe: value_type=text, or a null normalized (an unevaluated XLSX formula stub, a missing claim). Scale records how raw BECAME normalized -- where no normalized value was produced, nothing happened, and demanding a multiplier would force a fabricated one.

A qualitative claim is a text assertion by construction: typed text, no normalized magnitude, and it must name its assertion_class. Without this, claim_kind='qualitative' on a currency row would assert both extraction contracts at once.

SIM-375: enforce, not just describe, that `attribute` is canonical once E2 has run. attribute's own description already asserted this ('When E2 canonicalization has run, attribute_raw is then non-null, this is a canonical value') but nothing checked it -- $defs/canonicalAttribute was published and never referenced, so the stale-style camelCase names (or any string) still validated clean. attribute_raw present and non-null IS the E2-ran signal (see attribute_raw's own description); a claim that omits it or carries it null is pre-canonicalization or qualitative and keeps an unconstrained attribute, same as before.
